title: Pattern generator products and sharp left-anodyne inclusions
statement:
Let $\mathfrak P=(C,S,\{p_\alpha:K_\alpha^{\triangleleft}\to C\}_{\alpha\in A})$ be a small fully scaled categorical pattern, with the notation of [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy] and the marked-set conventions of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. Use the standard simplices, boundaries and horns from [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Define $J_{\mathfrak P}$ over $\bar C=(C,S)$ by the following seven generator types, including every base map satisfying the indicated condition:

(A0) $(\Lambda^2_1)^\sharp\amalg_{(\Lambda^2_1)^\flat}(\Delta^2)^\flat\longrightarrow(\Delta^2)^\sharp$, over every $\Delta^2\to C$ carrying all edges into $S$.

(A1) $Q^\flat\longrightarrow Q^\sharp$, where $Q=\Delta^0\amalg_{\Delta^{\{0,2\}}}\Delta^3\amalg_{\Delta^{\{1,3\}}}\Delta^0$ (both indicated edges are collapsed to vertices), over every $Q\to C$ carrying all edges into $S$.

(B0) $\{0\}^\sharp\longrightarrow(\Delta^1)^\sharp$, over every edge of $S$.

(B1) $K_\alpha^\sharp\longrightarrow(K_\alpha^{\triangleleft})^\sharp$, over $p_\alpha$, for every $\alpha\in A$.

(C0) $(\Lambda^n_0)^\flat\amalg_{(\Delta^{\{0,1\}})^\flat}(\Delta^{\{0,1\}})^\sharp\longrightarrow(\Delta^n)^\flat\amalg_{(\Delta^{\{0,1\}})^\flat}(\Delta^{\{0,1\}})^\sharp$, for every $n>1$ and every $\Delta^n\to C$ carrying the first edge into $S$.

(C1) $(\Lambda^n_i)^\flat\longrightarrow(\Delta^n)^\flat$, for $0<i<n$, over every $\Delta^n\to C$.

(C2) For $n\geq1$, $\alpha\in A$ and every $f:\Delta^n\star K_\alpha\to C$ restricting to $p_\alpha$ on $\{n\}\star K_\alpha$, take
$$ (\partial\Delta^n\star K_\alpha)^\flat\amalg_{(\{n\}\star K_\alpha)^\flat}(\{n\}\star K_\alpha)^\sharp\longrightarrow(\Delta^n\star K_\alpha)^\flat\amalg_{(\{n\}\star K_\alpha)^\flat}(\{n\}\star K_\alpha)^\sharp. $$

A weakly saturated closure is closure under pushouts, small transfinite compositions and retracts, including isomorphisms. For maps $r:X\to X'$ and $s:Y\to Y'$ define
$$r\mathbin\square s=(X'\times Y)\amalg_{X\times Y}(X\times Y')\longrightarrow X'\times Y'.$$

Let $J_0$ be the point-pattern subfamily consisting of (A0), (A1), (B0), (C0), and (C1) after taking $C=\Delta^0$ and $S$ to contain its unique edge; there are no (B1) or (C2) maps because the point pattern has no cones. Thus $J_0$ contains the initial marked edge inclusion $\{0\}^\sharp\to(\Delta^1)^\sharp$, the initial marked horns, and the inner marked horns. Write $W_{\mathfrak P}$ and $W_0$ for the weakly saturated closures of $J_{\mathfrak P}$ and $J_0$.

If $u:A\to A'$ is a degreewise injective marked map over $\bar C$ (injective in every simplicial degree) and $v:L\to L'$ is a degreewise injective marked map of simplicial sets, then

(a) $j\mathbin\square v\in W_{\mathfrak P}$ for every $j\in J_{\mathfrak P}$;

(b) $u\mathbin\square h\in W_{\mathfrak P}$ for every $h\in J_0$.

(c) If $a:U\hookrightarrow V$ is an ordinary left-anodyne inclusion (the weakly saturated closure of $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $n\geq1$, $0\leq i<n$), then $a^\sharp:U^\sharp\to V^\sharp$ belongs to $W_0$.

source.place: Higher Algebra Definition B.1.1, Proposition B.1.9 (all fourteen generator cases), and Lemma B.1.13, printed pp.1470-1482. P times the cone-free point pattern is P by Definition B.1.8. No Stacks tag states these marked infinity-categorical facts.

proof.text: First record the closure calculations used below. In marked simplicial sets a pushout has the degreewise simplicial pushout and the images of all input marked edges as its marking: giving a marking-preserving map out is exactly giving agreeing such maps on the two inputs. Increasing unions use the union marking. By [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells], an underlying monomorphism is built by boundary cells. Give each new simplex initially its flat marking, retaining every old marking, and then add each missing target marking by a pushout of $e:(\Delta^1)^\flat\to(\Delta^1)^\sharp$. Thus marked monomorphisms, including those over the base, are generated by $b_m:(\partial\Delta^m)^\flat\to(\Delta^m)^\flat$ and $e$, with all allowed structural maps. For a fixed map $r$, the construction $r\square-$ carries a pushout attachment to a pushout attachment and a continuous composite to the same relative continuous composite: degreewise, multiplication by a fixed set preserves the quotient presentation, with each relation imposed separately at each fixed coordinate. For markings the rule for marked products gives the same presentation on pairs of marked edges. Retracts are preserved functorially. Coproducts of attachments can be performed successively in a well-order. Consequently it suffices for (a) and (b) to check $b_m$ and $e$ in the arbitrary monomorphism variable.

source.place: B.1.9, reduction to the two generating cofibration families; explicit degreewise marked-colimit argument.

proof.text: Here is the inner-horn conversion used throughout. By [lem-coef-inner-horn-cell-generation], a map with the inner lifting-class property has a retract presentation by inner horn cells; conversely a map specified to be in their weakly saturated closure has such a horn-built description. Applying flat marking degreewise preserves pushouts, continuous composites and retract diagrams. Over an arbitrary fixed map of its codomain to $C$, every attaching flat inner horn is a generator (C1). Thus a flat inner-anodyne map, and every marked pushout of it, belongs to $W_{\mathfrak P}$. The same argument applies to $W_0$. This assertion uses no model structure on the pattern slice.

source.place: B.1.2 and the C1 cases in B.1.9.

proof.text: Check $j\square e$ for $j$ of type (A0) or (A1). More generally let $j:(X,M)\to(X,N)$ only add markings. Its product map is the identity on $X\times\Delta^1$. Its source already marks every horizontal edge $(a,0)$ and $(a,1)$ for $a\in N$, and every vertical edge at a vertex. For each still unmarked target edge $(a,01)$ use the triangle with vertices $(s(a),0),(t(a),0),(t(a),1)$, obtained from the degeneracy of $a$ and the interval. The consecutive edges are already marked, so a pushout of (A0) marks precisely this diagonal. Its base triangle is a degeneracy of the marked base edge of $a$, hence all edges lie in $S$. Mark all these diagonals successively. Every target marked edge is horizontal, vertical or one of these diagonals, so this gives the required map.

source.place: B.1.9, cases (A0),(A1) against the marking generator; explicit triangle attachments.

proof.text: For (B0) against $e$, the underlying square $\Delta^1\times\Delta^1$ is already present. The two horizontal edges and the vertical edge at the first vertex of the first factor are marked. Apply (A0) on the triangle $((0,0),(0,1),(1,1))$ to mark the diagonal. On the other triangle $((0,0),(1,0),(1,1))$, the first edge and the long edge are now marked. Apply assertion (i) of [lem-coef-pattern-marking-cancellation] to mark its remaining edge, the vertical edge at $1$. All base edges of both triangles are either the given edge in $S$ or degenerate. These are all the missing markings, so the product map lies in $W_{\mathfrak P}$.

source.place: B.1.9, case (B0) against the marking generator; B.1.11.

proof.text: For (B1) against $e$, write $v$ for the cone vertex. In $K_\alpha^{\triangleleft}\times\Delta^1$ every horizontal edge is initially marked, as are all edges lying in $K_\alpha\times\Delta^1$. For each vertex $k$ of $K_\alpha$, the triangle $((v,0),(k,0),(k,1))$ has both consecutive edges marked. A pushout of (A0) marks $(v,0)\to(k,1)$. The only remaining unmarked edge is $(v,0)\to(v,1)$. Map $\Delta^1\star K_\alpha$ to this product by taking its initial vertices to $(v,0),(v,1)$ and its $K_\alpha$ to $K_\alpha\times\{1\}$. Every edge except the initial one is now marked. The structural map carries all edges to $S$ and restricts to $p_\alpha$ on $\{1\}\star K_\alpha$. Assertion (ii) of [lem-coef-pattern-marking-cancellation] therefore marks the last edge. This also covers $K_\alpha=\varnothing$, when there are no preliminary triangles.

source.place: B.1.9, case (B1) against the marking generator; B.1.12.

proof.text: For (C0), (C1) and (C2) against $e$ the product is an isomorphism. Indeed every marked target edge and every vertex of the generating map is already in its source, with its marking: for (C0) this is the edge $01$, for (C1) just degenerate edges, and for (C2) the specified subcone $\{n\}\star K_\alpha$; here $n\geq1$ puts this subcone in $\partial\Delta^n\star K_\alpha$. Thus the source of the pushout product already contains every pair of marked edges of its target. Its underlying simplicial map is an identity because $e$ has identical source and target underneath.

source.place: B.1.9, cases (C) against the marking generator.

proof.text: Next check products with $b_m$. For $m=0$ the product is $j$ itself, in every generator case. Suppose $m>0$. For (A0) and (A1), the underlying product is again an identity. An edge marked in $X^\sharp\times(\Delta^m)^\flat$ has constant second coordinate, which is a vertex of $\partial\Delta^m$. All these markings already occur in the boundary factor of the pushout product. Hence these two cases are isomorphisms.

source.place: B.1.9, cases (A0 prime),(A1 prime), and the m=0 cases.

proof.text: For (B0) against $b_m$, use the prism pushouts in [lem-coef-infinity-right-prism-boundary], reversing the order in both factors and in the indexing simplices. Opposite simplicial sets merely precompose with the order-reversal automorphism of the simplex category; this operation preserves the degreewise pushout presentations. After identifying the reversed standard simplices with themselves, the initial subcomplex becomes $(\{0\}\times\Delta^m)\cup(\Delta^1\times\partial\Delta^m)$. At step $q=0,\ldots,m$ the attached simplex has vertices $(0,j)$ for $j\leq m-q$ and $(1,j-1)$ otherwise, and its horn index is $m-q$. For $q<m$ these are inner horns; at $q=m$ it is an initial horn whose first edge is the vertical edge over vertex $0$ of $\Delta^m$. The product marking consists of the edges with constant $\Delta^m$ coordinate. In each prism simplex the only nondegenerate such edge is the shuffle's vertical edge, and that edge already lies in the attaching horn; the boundary subcomplex supplies the corresponding edges at boundary vertices. Thus the inner cells use (C1) with flat marking, while the last cell uses (C0), whose distinguished first edge is marked and maps to the given edge of $S$. For $m=0$ the case is (B0) itself. Hence every stage is an allowed marked pushout, proving this case.

source.place: B.1.9, case (B0 prime); B.1.10 prism calculation.

proof.text: For (C0) against $b_m$, exchange the product factors and apply [lem-cbc-initial-prism-horn-filtration] with its parameters $m,n$. This supplies actual finite horn pushouts from the required union to $\Delta^m\times\Delta^n$, with every non-inner horn initial and its first edge equal to $((0,0),(0,1))$. Under the product marking this edge is marked and maps to the original edge $01$ in $S$. Use (C0) for those cells and (C1) for the inner cells. No target marked edge is lost: each has constant first coordinate and second edge $01$, already in $\Delta^m\times\Lambda_0^n$ with its marking. The cell pushout therefore has exactly the induced marking at each stage. This proves the marked product assertion, including $n=2$.

source.place: B.1.9, case (C0 prime); direct initial-horn prism route in place of the printed retract shorthand.

proof.text: For (C1) against $b_m$, its underlying map is the pushout product of an inner horn with a monomorphism. By [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product] it has the inner lifting-class property. Both product factors have flat marking, so its marking is flat. Step 2 makes it a member of $W_{\mathfrak P}$. The cited theorem concerns arbitrary unmarked simplicial sets and needs no fibrancy hypothesis.

For the remaining (B1) and (C2) products with $b_m$, assume $m>0$. Apply [lem-coef-relative-join-prism-comparison] with $K=K_\alpha$. For (B1) take $B=\Delta^0$, $A=\varnothing$; for (C2) take $B=\Delta^n$, $A=\partial\Delta^n$. Its $D$ is exactly the underlying source of the product, and its $T$ is the target. Every marked edge of $T$ has constant $\Delta^m$ coordinate, hence already belongs to $D$ because all vertices of $\Delta^m$ lie in $\partial\Delta^m$ for $m>0$; in the (C2) case the marked final subcone is also in $D$ because the final vertex $n$ belongs to $\partial\Delta^n$. Thus all subsequent underlying attachments may carry flat marking while retaining these old markings. By the cited comparison, $D\to Z$ is inner anodyne, so step 2 puts its marked version in $W_{\mathfrak P}$. The last stage is the pushout along $R\star K_\alpha\to(B\times\Delta^m)\star K_\alpha$ supplied by that same node, where $R=(A\times\Delta^m)\cup(B\times\partial\Delta^m)$.

source.place: B.1.9, cases (B1 prime),(C2 prime): inner comparison stages.

proof.text: Resolve that last join attachment explicitly. By [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells], attach the nondegenerate simplices of $B\times\Delta^m$ outside $R$ in dimension order, and join their attaching boundary with $K_\alpha$. Joining preserves these pushouts: each simplex splits uniquely into an initial leading block and a final $K_\alpha$ block, so the same degreewise relations present their joins. Any simplex outside $R$ projects surjectively to $\Delta^m$ and, in the (C2) case, to $\Delta^n$. Its final vertex is therefore $b=(v,m)$ in case (B1), or $b=(n,m)$ in case (C2). Every such simplex contains this final vertex, already in $R$ since $m>0$. Its dimension $d$ is at least one. Its join attachment is consequently a pushout of (C2) with that final vertex's subcone marked. That subcone maps to $p_\alpha$ under the structural map and is already marked in $D$: in case (B1) it is the copy of $K_\alpha^{\triangleleft}$ at $m$, and in case (C2) the given $\{n\}\star K_\alpha$ at $m$. No other new marking is imposed. Thus these attachments all lie in $W_{\mathfrak P}$. Their composite and the preceding inner stage prove both cone-product cases. No simplex of $K_\alpha$ is approximated by a finite cone shape.

source.place: B.1.9, final cone attachments; expands Example B.1.4.

proof.text: Steps 3-12 prove all fourteen generator/cofibration-generator cases of (a); the degreewise closure argument of step 1 proves (a) for every $v$. For (b), reduce $u$ by step 1 and exchange the product coordinates. There are only the five cone-free cases for $h$. Against the marking generator, use step 3 for (A0),(A1), step 4 for (B0), and step 6 for (C0),(C1). Against a boundary use step 7 for (A0),(A1), step 8 for (B0), step 9 for (C0), and step 10 for (C1). Check the structural maps to $C$: a boundary generator of $u$ is flat, so every marked edge in the product lies over a constant edge of its $\Delta^m$ factor. All (A0) and cancellation triangles are therefore constant over $C$, and the first edges of the initial-horn prism cells are constant over $C$, hence lie in $S$. When $u$ is the marking generator, its edge maps to $S$; each triangle used above is a degeneracy of that edge or is constant. Inner horns impose no restriction. Full scaling supplies every triangle condition. Thus these are actual $\mathfrak P$-generator pushouts over $C$, without treating arbitrary maps of $W_0$ as stable under pullback. Step 1 extends the result to every $u$.

source.place: B.1.9, symmetry and specialization of the second pattern to the cone-free point pattern.

proof.text: For (c), first take a generating left horn $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $0\leq i<n$. If $n>2$, the horn contains all edges. Push out (C1) when $i>0$, or (C0) when $i=0$, along the fully marked horn; its pushout marking is then sharp on the target. If $n=2,i=1$, pushing out (C1) along the sharp horn supplies a triangle with consecutive edges marked, and (A0) marks the last edge. If $n=2,i=0$, push out (C0) along the sharp horn, obtaining the triangle with edges $01,02$ marked, and use assertion (i) of [lem-coef-pattern-marking-cancellation] for the point pattern. If $n=1$ necessarily $i=0$ and the horn is the initial vertex $\{0\}$, giving (B0). Thus every generating sharp left horn is in $W_0$. Finally sharp marking preserves pushouts and continuous composites: every edge of the simplicial colimit is represented in an input and is therefore marked, with the usual universal property. It also preserves retract diagrams and isomorphisms. Applying it to any weakly saturated presentation of $a$ therefore puts $a^\sharp$ in $W_0$.

proof_origin.place: Proposition B.1.9 and Lemma B.1.13, read online; archival copy unavailable locally. Explicit marking attachments, relative join comparison, and existing prism nodes replace shorthand identifications. No pattern model structure is used.
